title: Identity and Access Implementation Reference
readerIntent: Locate identity, authentication, authorization, browser-session, migration, and extension responsibilities precisely.
owner: Profile, nAuth, nToken, nRouter, nCache, and each target module according to responsibility
summary: Profile owns persisted identity and tenancy; nAuth owns reusable authentication security; nToken owns generic token mechanics; nRouter applies route policy; nCache supplies strict shared state; target modules own operation and data authorization.

sections.heading: Quick decision matrix
items: Use employee username/password only for human BackOffice authentication, customer credentials only for consumer login, and service principals for module or scheduled access.
A route declares accepted token class and permissions; schema and ownership policy further narrow records and fields.
Tenant context is mandatory and cannot be broadened by request values. Cross-tenant service work requires explicit separate authority.
Frontend visibility is guidance only. The target backend route and owning service always make the final decision.

sections.heading: Authority map
items: Profile: tenants, enterprises, people, employees, customers, service principals, groups, credentials, contacts, addresses, authentication state, browser-session facade, identity bootstrap, and governed identity migration.
nAuth: JWT security, API-key digest policy, service-token issuance, security stamps, principal/group governance configuration, strict auth activation, and reusable authentication contracts.
nToken: generic token mechanics; it does not own persisted people or business authorization.
nRouter: route exposure, token-type restrictions through authTokenTypes, permissions, tenant resolution, request pipeline, controller dispatch, and response handling.
nCache: provider-neutral shared authentication-state operations including atomic consume; strict modular deployments require a qualified distributed engine and disabled local fallback.
Target module: route permission, schema action/group access, fields, ownership, relationships, business validation, audit, and data.

sections.heading: Configuration and extension
items: Configure JWT issuer, audience, algorithms, lifetimes, secret, API-key pepper, service-token permission, security stamps, identity governance, bootstrap identity, strict cache channel, and browser sessions through the layered properties/runtime contracts.

Reusable Profile schema policies live under schemaPolicies.profile; identity principal, registration, groups, permission catalog, migration, and separation-of-duties rules remain named configurable contributions.
Project modules extend configuration and owned schemas/services in later layers; never embed project group names in framework routes or closure constants inside schemas.
Use authTokenTypes to make a route service-only or otherwise explicitly constrain accepted authenticated token classes.
Do not add a parallel identity store, token issuer, permission registry, session cache path, browser refresh implementation, or database access path.

sections.heading: Browser endpoints
items: POST /nodics/profile/v0/employee/browser/authenticate
POST /nodics/profile/v0/employee/browser/restore
POST /nodics/profile/v0/employee/browser/logout
Access tokens stay in client memory; refresh credentials stay in scoped HttpOnly cookies; restore/logout require exact allowed Origin and CSRF proof.

sections.heading: Lifecycle and failure
items: Username/password login resolves enterprise/tenant before credential validation but is separate from secured module-to-module token retrieval.
Principal/password/group changes advance security stamps and invalidate affected human and service tokens through shared tenant-scoped state.
Group inheritance must be active, acyclic, and limited to catalogued permissions; descendant membership changes invalidate impacted sessions.
Fail closed on missing/weak secrets, missing tenant, untrusted stamp state, invalid scope/audience/type, permission denial, unavailable atomic consume, or unsafe local fallback.
Identity migration uses permissioned preview, apply, repeat, fail, and rollback with redacted audit; rollback never restores plaintext credentials.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Run focused Profile and nAuth contracts, the auth P2 suite, and the required live Redis release gate for production qualification.
Cover positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, distributed-race, security, performance, provider outage, recovery, upgrade, and regression behavior.

Verify customer registration cannot assign privileged groups/permissions/API keys, service-only routes reject human tokens, tenant boundaries hold across modules, browser refresh is single-use, and logs/audit remain credential-free.

sections.heading: What This Capability Does
paragraphs: Enterprise search gives an authorized employee a safe way to find enterprise records for administrative work. Typical examples are selecting an enterprise before creating related data, confirming whether an enterprise is active, or asking Axis Assistant to find an enterprise by code.

Profile remains the business, validation, authorization, and persistence owner. BackOffice supplies current contract discovery, while Assistant supplies conversation and governed tool orchestration. Neither stores a second enterprise list.

Confirmed creation is exposed separately at `POST /nodics/profile/v0/enterprises`. It requires a human access token, `profile.enterprise.create`, bounded input, and an idempotency key. Profile checks duplicate code and uses the generated `DefaultEnterpriseService`; an AI module never writes the enterprise collection directly. Axis Assistant first creates and approves an immutable confirmation, then calls Profile or hands the approved work to Workflow.

sections.heading: Business User Workflow
paragraphs: An authorized employee may search without filters to receive the first bounded page, or use exact filters:

```text
GET /nodics/profile/v0/enterprises/search?code=default
GET /nodics/profile/v0/enterprises/search?name=Default%20Enterprise&active=true
GET /nodics/profile/v0/enterprises/search?page=2&limit=25
```

The result contains `page`, `limit`, `count`, and `items`. Each item may contain the configured safe fields such as enterprise code, name, active state, tenant code, parent-enterprise code, and timestamps.

Expected rejected journeys include an employee without the permission, a customer or service credential, an unknown/operator filter, an invalid active value, or pagination beyond the configured boundary. Correct the credential, permission, or filter and retry. There is no partial write or rollback because this operation is read-only.

sections.heading: Axis Assistant Workflow
paragraphs: The inactive OOTB `axisAssistantReadOnly` policy allowlists the logical tool `profile.enterprise.search`. A project or local environment may activate a reviewed layered policy. At execution time:

Model output cannot choose a URL, HTTP method, credential, permission result, or unapproved response field.

For confirmed creation, the employee first selects an existing unassigned tenant or completes the separately governed tenant-creation process. An enterprise owns one tenant under the current Profile schema, so attempting to associate a tenant that already belongs to another enterprise is rejected by the Profile management service before persistence and remains protected by the authoritative unique tenant database contract. The enterprise record itself is stored through Profile's configured default enterprise store; `tenantCode` is the business association and must not be used as a second database-model selection path.

Axis Assistant binds the operation, arguments, employee, tenant context, expiry, revision, and idempotency key into `assistantConfirmation`. Changed arguments or replay return conflict, expired confirmations return gone, and unsupported mutations return bad request. Direct execution forwards the human bearer to Profile. When `workflowCode` is selected, Assistant creates an active Workflow item and returns a durable carrier code; Workflow, not Assistant, owns all later manual or automatic actions.

sections.heading: Configuration
paragraphs: Layer the smallest required fragment instead of copying Profile:

Smaller result bounds or a smaller projection are safe customizations. Adding a field requires a disclosure review and tests. Do not add credentials, contacts, addresses, unrestricted metadata, or recursive references.

sections.heading: Architecture And Data Contract
paragraphs: The router delegates to `DefaultEnterpriseManagementController`, then `DefaultEnterpriseManagementFacade`, then `DefaultEnterpriseManagementService`. The service calls the existing generated `DefaultEnterpriseService` with the configured default enterprise tenant, caller authentication evidence, exact filters, `recursive: false`, stable code sorting, and bounded pagination.

The enterprise schema and generated service remain authoritative. This design does not use nSearch or Elasticsearch because the implemented filters are bounded exact database queries and Profile search indexing is not enabled. If a future measured requirement needs full-text search, extend the existing nSearch authority rather than adding a second index.

sections.heading: Partner Extension Example
paragraphs: A partner that needs a non-sensitive `regionCode` may add it to the enterprise schema through the normal later module layer, add it to layered `projectedFields`, update the disclosure documentation, and extend the focused projection test. The partner must not copy the enterprise model, create an Assistant-owned enterprise collection, or bypass Profile permissions.
